newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to OK Taiwan stock index-futures in Oct '97.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to OK Taiwan stock index-futures in Oct '97.

text.p: Taiwan regulators will allow trading on Taiwan stock index-linked futures and derivatives planned to be launched by exchanges in Chicago and Singapore in October 1997, the United Daily News reported on Sunday.

The newspaper quoted the Securities and Exchange Commission's chairman Lu Tung-ying as saying the commission would authorise the two foreign exchanges for Taiwan stock index-linked futures in July 1997, and then allow trading to begin in October 1997.

Lu was quoted as saying legislation of the Futures Trading Law needed to be completed by the end of 1996. Simultaneous introduction of the domestic Taiwan stock index-futures with the two foreign exchanges is also required.
A draft of the law is under parliament screening.

The commission, which oversees development of Taiwan's own futures exchange, has faced heavy pressure to swiftly establish the exchange after the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) and Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX) said recently they would launch Taiwan stock index-linked futures.

The CME and SIMEX, eyeing a gap opened by Taiwan's financial liberalisation but not yet filled by the long-awaited Taiwan futures exchange, have announced plans to launch Taiwan stock-index futures and options in January.

A commission spokeswoman said on Saturday the commission would set up the island's first futures trading exchange in October 1997, delayed from the originally scheduled July 1997 due to failure to complete all preparatory work.
Officials at the commission were not immediately available to comment.
